change_summary: Added an experiment-only runtime risk multiplier hook for `breakout_long` and screened a minimal self-cooldown family on the deterministic late / mid / old snapshots. The rule looked only at the most recent closed breakout trades already visible before each new entry and, when the recent breakout sleeve had a fully losing lookback with non-positive aggregate PnL, shrank new breakout risk to `0.0x`, `0.25x`, or `0.5x`. The code was rolled back after the sweep failed the majority-window test.

delta_metrics.note: No screened variant produced a majority-window EV gain. Harsh cooldowns improved the oldest weak window slightly but destroyed the mid window, while milder cooldowns mostly regressed the mid window and left the old window unchanged. The strong recent window stayed a null because the breakout sleeve never entered the required losing streak there.

hypothesis: If `breakout_long` is a regime-sensitive convex sleeve rather than a stationary alpha source, then one possible runtime defense is to de-risk new breakouts whenever the sleeve itself has already closed several consecutive losing trades. A short realized-loss cooldown might reduce exposure in weak breakout phases without touching trend logic or entry selection.

market_regime_summary.mid_weak: ripping bull / high-beta leadership but strategy lags broad beta materially
market_regime_summary.old_thin: mixed-to-weak tape where breakout is fragile and trend is the only modestly persistent sleeve

next_retry_requires: Do not revisit breakout health using only the sleeve's own last-few-trades PnL as the state variable
If breakout-health conditioning is revisited, require a forward-looking context source observable before entry, such as market breadth / participation quality or another tape-quality proxy
Do not treat small improvement in the oldest weak window as sufficient; this branch must prove it can avoid damaging the mid window where breakout still has meaningful upside
notes: The experiment changed one causal variable only: runtime breakout risk based on recent closed breakout losses. The temporary code was removed after measurement, so the repository trading logic remains unchanged.

parameters.trigger: recent closed breakout trades count >= lookback AND all counted trades are losers AND summed breakout pnl <= 0

rejection_reason: Rejected on multi-window stability. A lagging self-cooldown based only on the breakout sleeve's recent realized losses is too late and too blunt: it cuts future breakout convexity in windows where recoveries still matter, while offering only marginal relief in the oldest weak window. The mechanism does not provide a stable majority-window alpha improvement.
